title: What Burns in the Hollow
author: unsigned, House Maervaine
pages: The children of the sun say a beast swallowed the Dawn. We were there. We say this once, in writing, for the House alone. No beast swallowed her. She fell, and we were the reason.

When the Starwrights drew her down, she burned through the floor of the world and broke the edge of the sky. She did not die. A star does not die so easily. She went mad in the dark, and the dark woke.
We could not lift her back. So we bound her where she lay, at the rim of the Hollow, and fed her light with the Lanterns, and the Lanterns with ourselves. Her light holds the Unlit asleep.
Held so long in the dark, she grew wings and scales and hunger. The Tall Ones call her mistress. The sun-children call her Star-Eater. She is not the one who ate the Dawn. She is the Dawn.

Whoever slays her will not free her. They will put out the last of her light, the Unlit will stir, and the Night will come. If she must die, let the Last Ember be rekindled before the dark grows bold.
Do not tell the Sunthrones. Do not tell the young. Do not tell anyone who would weep, or hope. Burn any copy outside the House. We have paid enough. Let someone else pay the next time.
